_provenance.source: User Manual for the Short-Stay 'Schengen' Calculator, European Commission, Section 6 'Examples'
_provenance.note: Worked examples transcribed from the official manual. Our engine must match the official calculator on all of them (AGENTS.md §6.6). Expected values below are stated verbatim in the manual; derived fields (exact exit dates) follow arithmetically from the manual's day counts.

example1.description: Person not subject to the visa requirement: enters 1 Jan 2024 and leaves same day; enters again 1 Jun 2024 and stays until 20 Sep 2024.

statusCases.manualText: On 14.6.2024: over the last 180 days (18.12.2023 - 14.6.2024) the person had stayed 1 day + 14 days = 15 days; no overstay.
On 29.8.2024: over the last 180 days (3.3.2024 - 29.8.2024) the person had stayed 90 days (1.6.2024 - 29.8.2024); 29.8.2024 = last day of authorised stay.

planCase.manualText: 29.8.2024 is the last day of authorised stay for the stay begun 1.6.2024, so staying until 20.9.2024 is an overstay beginning 30.8.2024.

example2.description: Visa holder (90/180 multiple-entry visa): stays 1-10 Jan 2024 (10 days), 1-30 Mar 2024 (30 days), 1 May - 9 Jun 2024 (40 days).

maxStayCases.manualText: On 19.6.2024: the person might enter for a consecutive 20 days maximum (10 leftover days 19-28.6, plus 10 days as the 1-10 Jan stay rolls out of the window from 29.6).
On 7.8.2024: still 20 consecutive days maximum; on 26.8.2024 the person should leave, reaching 90 days in the window.
On 8.8.2024: the person might enter for a consecutive 50 days maximum (10 leftover + 10 from the January stay + 30 from the March stay rolling out from 28.8).
On 8.9.2024: the person might enter for a consecutive 90 days maximum; 90 days of absence (10.6.2024 - 7.9.2024) always allows a new 90-day stay.
